record.paper_title: Higher Rank Brill-Noether Theory and Coherent Systems: Open Questions
record.context_brief: Flip loci and cohomology on P^1
record.original_question: Can one explicitly determine the flip loci for coherent systems of type (n,d,k) on P^1 and use them to compute the Hodge and Poincare polynomials of the chamber moduli spaces G_i(n,d,k)?

evidence.quote: Question 6.3. Can one determine the flip loci for coherent systems of type (n, d, k) on P1 and use this information to compute Hodge and Poincaré polynomials of Gi(n, d, k)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{P}^1$ be the complex projective line. A coherent system of type $(n,d,k)$ on $\mathbb{P}^1$ is a pair $(E,V)$ where $E$ is a holomorphic vector bundle of rank $n$ and degree $d$ on $\mathbb{P}^1$ and $V \subseteq H^0(\mathbb{P}^1,E)$ is a $k$-dimensional linear subspace of global sections. For a real parameter $\alpha > 0$, the $\alpha$-slope of $(E,V)$ is defined by
$$\mu_\alpha(E,V) = \frac{d}{n} + \alpha \frac{k}{n},$$
and $(E,V)$ is called $\alpha$-(semi)stable if for every proper coherent subsystem $(E',V') \subset (E,V)$ with $0 < \operatorname{rk}(E') < n$ one has $\mu_\alpha(E',V') < \mu_\alpha(E,V)$ (resp. $\le$). The moduli space of $\alpha$-stable coherent systems of type $(n,d,k)$ on $\mathbb{P}^1$ is denoted $G_\alpha(n,d,k)$.

As $\alpha$ varies over $(0,\infty)$, there is a finite set of critical values $0 < \alpha_1 < \alpha_2 < \cdots < \alpha_L$ at which the moduli space changes; on each open chamber $(\alpha_{i-1},\alpha_i)$ the moduli space is constant, denoted $G_i(n,d,k)$. At each critical value $\alpha_i$, the difference between the moduli spaces on adjacent chambers is concentrated on the so-called flip loci, the subvarieties parametrizing coherent systems that are stable on one side of $\alpha_i$ but unstable on the other.

Problem. For all admissible triples $(n,d,k)$ with $n \ge 2$, $k \ge 1$, give an explicit description of the flip loci at every critical value $\alpha_i$ for coherent systems of type $(n,d,k)$ on $\mathbb{P}^1$, and use this description to compute the Hodge polynomial and the Poincaré polynomial of each chamber moduli space $G_i(n,d,k)$.
artifact.category_tag: moduli of coherent systems on curves
artifact.status_search_result: The case $k=1$ has been carried out: Lange–Newstead ("Coherent systems of genus 0, III: Computation of flips for $k=1$", arXiv:0707.1466) determine the flip loci and compute Hodge polynomials of $G_i(n,d,1)$ explicitly for ranks 2 and 3 and in certain cases for arbitrary rank. For general $k \ge 2$ on $\mathbb{P}^1$, no complete explicit determination of the flip loci or the resulting Hodge/Poincaré polynomials of $G_i(n,d,k)$ appears in the literature, so the problem is only partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Coherent systems of genus 0, III: Computation of flips for k=1
status_evidence.snippet: Determines inductively the first and last moduli spaces and the flip loci for coherent systems of type (n,d,1) on P^1, with explicit Hodge polynomials for ranks 2 and 3.
status_evidence.claim: The k=1 case is treated, providing flip loci and Hodge polynomials of G_i(n,d,1).

status_evidence.title: Higher rank Brill–Noether theory and coherent systems: open questions
status_evidence.snippet: Lists Question 6.3 on flip loci and Hodge/Poincaré polynomials of G_i(n,d,k) on P^1 as an open question.
status_evidence.claim: The general (n,d,k) version is posed as an open question.
